prompt:
Since the number of workspaces grew past a few dozen, the background work has become unreliable:

1. Many workspaces no longer get "issue overdue" alerts, even though they have open issues that are past due. Which workspaces are affected changes over time. Workspaces that are left out on one run are often left out on the next run as well.
2. The daily digest email has the same problem. Members who opted into the digest and have unread notifications get nothing on the day their workspace is skipped.
3. The retention cleanup that drops expired archived content from search leaves some workspaces untouched for weeks.
4. The periodic usage recount (it corrects the issue, project and seat counters that the billing page and the plan checks read) keeps recounting the same workspaces over and over. The counters of the other workspaces drift and are never corrected.
5. A workspace that was deleted still triggers "issue overdue" alerts.

Expected behaviour: every run of the overdue alerts, the daily digest and the retention cleanup must cover every workspace that has not been deleted, however many workspaces there are, and each run must still behave as it does today for each workspace it covers (for example, an overdue issue is still announced only once, and a digest is not sent twice). A deleted workspace gets no overdue alerts and no digest. The usage recount stays incremental on purpose: each run recounts at most 25 workspaces, and it picks the ones whose counters were recounted longest ago. A recounted workspace moves to the back of the queue. The small counter adjustments recorded whenever something is created or removed do not count as a recount, and they must not change a workspace's place in the queue.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Root causes (shared work list in the usage repository, consumed by four jobs). Injected (bug.patch, repository): listOrgIdsForRollup now orders by measured_at DESC, with a docstring arguing that the most recently measured tenants are the ones drifting; the rollup job's batch comment was adjusted to match. So a recount (which stamps measured_at) puts a workspace straight back at the head of the list, and the rollup recounts the same 25 forever. Latent in pristine: (a) the overdue, digest and cleanup sweeps reuse that bounded rollup list (batches of 50/50/25, ordered by usage activity), so with more tenants than the batch some workspaces are never swept; (b) incrementUsage, the write-path delta behind every create/archive event, also bumps measured_at, so a write reorders the recount queue; (c) the overdue sweep does not skip deleted (archived) workspaces. The digest sweep does. Reference fix (7 files, +66/-33): organization-repository gets a keyset-paged listLiveOrgIds; jobs/types gets forEachLiveOrg; the overdue, digest and cleanup jobs iterate all live orgs with it; incrementUsage stops touching measured_at; the rollup list goes back to least-recently-recounted first (tie-break on org id). Why hard: the symptoms are in four jobs and three features (alerts, email, search retention, billing counters). They depend on tenant count and activity, and the jobs look individually correct. Reverting the sort alone still starves sweeps and lets writes reorder the recount. Pointing the sweeps at an unbounded list is needed, but the rollup must stay bounded (25) and fair, which the hidden test pins with 30 tenants and a write order unrelated to recount order. A sweep over all orgs must exclude deleted ones. Validation: bug -> git apply clean, tsc 0, visible 617/617; hidden 6/9 fail; bug+solution -> hidden 9/9, full 626/626, tsc 0; naive A (revert the sort only) -> 6/9 fail; naive B (rollup fully fixed, sweeps untouched) -> 4/9 fail; naive C (sweeps + sort fixed, incrementUsage still bumps measured_at) -> 2/9 fail; hidden x3 stable.
